children: The rupee opened 11 paise lower on August 31, after the United States Federal Reserve stated on Friday that the likelihood of a rate hike is not so far away, should inflation keep spiking towards the target of 2 percent, striking a hawkish tone.
The local currency was trading at Rs 95.49 per dollar, as compared to Rs 95.38 per dollar in the previous trading session.

US Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s comments in a closely watched speech on Friday have now raised the possibility of a rate hike in September, according to the CME Fed Watch tool. The odds of a rate hike increased to 60 percent after the speech, up from 35 percent before.

Additonally, the rupee came in under marginal pressure, after Brent crude prices made their way back to the $90 per barrel mark, after the US attacked Iranian rocket launchers near the Strait of Hormuz, the first such strike in almost a month.
Today also marks the end of the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) special foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposit scheme, which pulled in more than $65 billion in fresh dollar inflows.

“In the near term, Rs 95.10 to Rs 95.30 will act as a strong support zone, with close to a 90 percent chance the pair holds here. On the resistance side, the Rs 95.80 per dollar level is key,” Amit Pabari, managing director at CR Forex Advisors, said.

title: Rupee opens 11 paise lower to Rs 95.49 per dollar, US Fed strikes hawkish tone
